description: This figure group is a single image: a table (no micrograph, curve or schematic panel, no scale bar or axis) reporting the multilevel martensitic structural characteristics of two steels. The header row has five columns: "Steel", "d_a/μm", "d_p/μm", "d_b/μm" and "d_l/μm", i.e. average sizes of prior austenite grains (d_a), martensitic packets (d_p), martensitic blocks (d_b) and martensitic laths (d_l) in micrometres. Row 1, steel "0Al", gives 26.1 ± 9.4, 3.4 ± 0.8, 0.9 ± 0.2, 0.24 ± 0.07. Row 2, steel "1.3Al", gives 23.4 ± 5.9, 3.5 ± 0.9, 0.8 ± 0.2, 0.23 ± 0.06. Every entry is a mean with a standard deviation. Within each steel the structural scale decreases monotonically from prior austenite grain through packet and block to lath. Comparing the two steels, 1.3Al has the smaller prior austenite grain size (23.4 vs 26.1 μm) and a much smaller spread (±5.9 vs ±9.4 μm), slightly smaller blocks and laths, and a marginally larger packet size (3.5 vs 3.4 μm). The table demonstrates that 1.3Al addition refines the prior austenite grain size while leaving the finer martensitic substructure essentially unchanged.

subfigures.description: A five-column, two-data-row table of multilevel martensitic structural sizes for steels 0Al and 1.3Al; columns are Steel, d_a/μm, d_p/μm, d_b/μm, d_l/μm, each cell a mean ± standard deviation.
